authorship: Original Video Forge synthesis; cited sources inform mechanisms, not copied templates

recipes.name: A detail earns its wide reveal
assets: product geometry or exact product still
recipes.visualArgument: Open on an interpretable detail, move past a near edge, then reveal the whole object and its use.
recipes.camera: Three-quarter detail → lateral dolly with foreground parallax → stable hero. Keep the target on the relevant feature, then widen the target with the reveal.
recipes.rhythm: A short accelerating travel lands before the claim; hold the hero while the viewer reads.
recipes.transition: Carry a silhouette or highlight across a cut; avoid a whole-film orbit.
recipes.sound: Material-specific foley at the reveal; a restrained low hit at the landing.
do: Show product identity rather than an anonymous glossy blob
Match lighting and scale to the real asset
avoid: Do not spin solely to fill time
Do not put exact UI copy on a grazing unreadable plane

recipes.name: Travel through a relationship
recipes.visualArgument: Move from fragmented stations toward one coherent output; the camera route is the explanation.
recipes.camera: Establish a near/mid/far relationship. Truck or dolly past occluders toward a clear endpoint; maintain a stable horizon and look target.
recipes.rhythm: Continuous velocity through intermediate points; decelerate only when arriving at the important result.
recipes.transition: Hide a change behind a full passing edge, matching travel direction and speed.
recipes.sound: Air/space movement can build through the journey; stop the bed or accent at the payoff.
do: Give stations distinct roles
Leave a proof hold after travel
avoid: Do not use a generic endless tunnel for every product
Do not fly through the only readable evidence

recipes.name: Show what contributes to the result
recipes.visualArgument: Separate a useful system into its contributing parts, show their roles, then make the assembled consequence visible.
recipes.camera: A modest arc reveals thickness and ordering; camera movement and part separation run on separate tracks.
recipes.rhythm: Separate → brief analysis hold → reassemble with a stable final state.
recipes.transition: An assembled edge can match into the actual product or UI; preserve topology/roles.
recipes.sound: Distinct small placement sounds, one final lock; avoid a pop on every minor object.
do: Use actual component roles
Preserve a readable silhouette
avoid: Do not scatter parts randomly
Do not claim a procedural proxy is a real product model

recipes.name: Show the result, then the decisive action
recipes.visualArgument: Begin with an observable result; reveal the action responsible and its consequence.
recipes.camera: Frontal readable proof. A short push to the relevant control, then a return to a useful context; a browser frame is optional.
recipes.rhythm: Fast context changes around a longer proof hold; preserve the visible action order.
recipes.transition: Match a real selected element or mask to the next relevant view.
recipes.sound: Use a click or state-change cue only where a visible action occurs.
do: Inspect real captures
Distinguish recorded interaction from illustrative cursors
avoid: Do not shrink a whole desktop page into a tiny box
Do not fabricate private dashboard success

recipes.name: A person makes a promise; evidence answers it
recipes.visualArgument: Use the strongest complete question/result first, then show proof under the continuing voice and return for a human payoff.
recipes.camera: Vary medium/detail and deliberate punch-ins; keep eyes/hands clear and the crop stable through gestures.
recipes.rhythm: Paper cut on meaning; use an L cut under proof and a J cut to pull the next scene forward.
recipes.transition: Cut on gesture or sound when possible; a hard cut often communicates best.
recipes.sound: Dialogue and room continuity first, selective sound punctuation second.
do: Retain qualifiers and approved order
Choose a cutaway that proves the spoken point
avoid: Do not threshold-cut every breath
Do not cover the entire speaker with redundant headline captions

recipes.name: Let real actions carry the edit
recipes.visualArgument: Show a process through a few causally connected actions and the actual result.
recipes.camera: Alternate useful wider orientation and detail; match hand/tool travel across the cut.
recipes.rhythm: Cut inside useful movement; allow a result to settle before another action.
recipes.transition: Carry direction, shape or a material surface between actions.
recipes.sound: Use source foley/room tone; music accents reinforce rather than replace action.
do: Check action continuity
Preserve original speed where it demonstrates the skill
avoid: Do not use unrelated stock hands as proof
Do not hide a missing step with a flash

recipes.name: Build a distinct visual argument from cast material
recipes.visualArgument: Organize a point of view through contrast, crop and hierarchy; let the assets do more work than UI cards.
recipes.camera: Mostly stable graphic composition with deliberate crop changes; use depth only when it reveals a relationship.
recipes.rhythm: Vary a dense image burst with a clean decisive phrase and a proof hold.
recipes.transition: Use matching edges, masks or type alignment instead of unrelated preset zooms.
recipes.sound: A coherent percussive palette with intentional empty beats.
do: Cast assets with consistent light/material or an intentional collage logic
Keep one dominant read
avoid: Do not combine random stock styles by accident
Do not animate every layer equally

recipes.name: Move through a layered image honestly
recipes.visualArgument: A modest camera-like move reveals depth and directs attention inside a still.
recipes.camera: Use different layer depth/speed and a foreground overlap; this remains 2.5D, not a volumetric product scan.
recipes.rhythm: A short move then a stable subject hold; keep edges and newly exposed regions clean.
recipes.transition: Match the important subject or dissolve at a stable moment.
recipes.sound: Atmospheric source-appropriate sound rather than an impact on every layer.
do: Inspect cutout edges and filled regions
Keep movement within available image coverage
avoid: Do not expose empty holes behind cutouts
Do not label 2.5D parallax as true 3D reconstruction

recipes.name: Make the supplied change visible
recipes.visualArgument: Show an initial state, apply one cause, and reveal the resulting change using the same visual language.
recipes.camera: Use a frontal or modest spatial view that preserves value comparison; camera can reveal scale after the values read.
recipes.rhythm: Animate the change, hold the comparison, then isolate its implication.
recipes.transition: Maintain a shape/value anchor through the transition.
recipes.sound: One cue for the causal event; let the result breathe.
do: Preserve exact values and units
Show evidence before an interpretive claim
avoid: Do not imply fake statistics
Do not use perspective to distort a comparison

recipes.name: Typography performs the idea
recipes.visualArgument: Use words as spatial objects whose behavior makes the statement understandable.
recipes.camera: Stable view for reading; a decisive reframe can reveal a changed relation between words.
recipes.rhythm: Anticipate → transform → settle; vary word rhythm around actual speech.
recipes.transition: Carry a letter edge, underline, or word position into the next concept.
recipes.sound: Emphasize the decisive phrase rather than every syllable.
do: Choose motion semantically
Keep settled text readable at phone size
avoid: Do not use type as a substitute for missing proof
Do not combine unrelated headline and subtitle sentences at equal weight

recipes.name: Compress travel, protect the action
recipes.visualArgument: Speed through connective travel, arrive at the meaningful action, and preserve the result.
recipes.camera: A matched direction or occluder can support the ramp; stabilize the important landing.
recipes.rhythm: Change speed around actual movement; normal-speed payoff and selective detail hold.
recipes.transition: Use motion continuity or an occlusion cut rather than a generic flash.
recipes.sound: Preserve intentional foley timing; ramps should not distort crucial speech.
do: Check source frame rate
Inspect interpolation artifacts through the whole action
avoid: Do not invent missing high-speed frames
Do not ramp the only proof into unreadability

recipes.name: Direct a small coherent coverage set
recipes.visualArgument: A contextual view, useful detail/action and consequence form one consistent visual story.
recipes.camera: One principal camera move per take, anchored start/end framing and screen direction.
recipes.rhythm: Use short selected takes with enough handles; trim on the actual usable action.
recipes.transition: Match direction/light/material across generated shots and deterministic graphics.
recipes.sound: Sound is separately selected/designed unless the provider actually returns usable audio.
do: Keep continuity anchors stable
Inspect complete takes, not only first frames
avoid: Do not claim endpoint success equals visual quality
Do not reroll blindly after an ambiguous paid request
